en.summary: Costa Rica has one of the most open media environments in Latin America. La Nación, the leading daily, belongs to Grupo Nación, which also publishes La Teja and the business weekly El Financiero. Digital-native CRHoy is among the most read sites, and the television channels Teletica and Repretel lead broadcast news. Semanario Universidad, published by the University of Costa Rica, is known for investigative reporting. The Tico Times covers the country in English. Most news sites are free to read; La Nación uses a metered paywall.

faq.q: What are the main national news outlets in Costa Rica?
faq.a: The main national outlets in the directory include La Nación, CRHoy, Teletica and Diario Extra. The Top National News column lists them in editorial order.

faq.q: Is there Costa Rican news in English?
faq.a: The Tico Times covers Costa Rica in English. Its language is shown in the directory.

faq.q: Where can I find regional news in Costa Rica?
faq.a: Regional coverage in the directory comes from La Voz de Guanacaste. The Regional & Local column lists every regional outlet.

general-news.intro: Costa Rica's national outlets are based in San José and combine a leading daily, digital sites and television news.

economy.intro: Business news in Costa Rica comes from a business weekly and regional magazines covering companies, trade and investment.

broadcast.intro: Television and radio remain major news sources in Costa Rica. The channels and stations below publish their newscasts online.
